thesis: Snowflake is the leading cloud-agnostic data platform, and the deeply-oversold recovery thesis has fully played out — shares have roughly doubled from ~$119 (RSI ~16) to ~$273 on sustained 30%+ growth, positive free cash flow, and accelerating AI Data Cloud adoption. FY2026 total revenue rose 29.2% to $4.68B, TTM revenue is ~$5.03B (+31%), NRR is ~125%, and RPO is ~$9.8B, while FCF runs ~$1.2B+ at a ~25% margin. Cortex AI and Snowflake Intelligence are the core growth engines, and a 51-analyst Strong Buy consensus (avg target ~$297.60) reflects a profitable-cash-flow quality leader rather than a speculative bounce. The upgrade to BUY drops the speculative tag; the principal caution is a full valuation (~129x forward earnings, heavy stock-based comp) that leaves only modest near-term upside.

drivers: Cortex AI and Snowflake Intelligence adoption accelerates consumption growth back above 30%
Net Revenue Retention re-expands toward 130% as AI workloads scale
FCF margin expands beyond 25% while non-GAAP operating margin keeps climbing
Multiple post-run target raises validate momentum (BofA $330, KeyBanc $325, Jefferies $310)
Databricks' ~$188B private valuation reframes public SNOW as relatively undervalued

base_case.assumptions: Revenue compounds ~25–30% through FY2028 with steady margin expansion and ~25% FCF margins; Cortex/Snowflake Intelligence contribute meaningfully but do not re-accelerate growth dramatically; NRR holds around 125%; the stock tracks toward the ~$297.60 consensus average target as earnings confirm the AI Data Cloud ramp.

risks: Databricks (new funding at ~$188B, expanded ~$100M OpenAI deal) and Microsoft Fabric take AI-workload share
Consumption-revenue model volatility drives a guidance miss and multiple compression from ~129x forward earnings
Heavy stock-based compensation keeps GAAP losses large and dilutes shareholders
AI-momentum enthusiasm fades and the stock retraces toward its prior range
Growth decelerates below the mid-20s% as the law of large numbers bites

catalysts.event: Q2 FY2027 earnings — revenue growth, margins, and updated FY2027 guidance
Cortex AI and Snowflake Intelligence adoption metrics — the core growth driver to watch
Net Revenue Retention trajectory — signal of consumption expansion vs. deceleration
Competitive dynamics vs. Databricks and Microsoft Fabric in AI-data workloads

key_risks: Full valuation (~129x forward earnings) leaves only ~9% average-target upside and limited margin for error
Intensifying AI-workload competition from Databricks (~$188B private valuation, expanded OpenAI deal) and Microsoft Fabric
Consumption-based revenue model creates quarter-to-quarter volatility during enterprise budget swings
Heavy stock-based compensation keeps GAAP results in the red and dilutes shareholders
CEO pay package worth up to ~$448M tied to the stock doubling adds an alignment/governance and dilution consideration
